inner_monologue_engine.name: Inner Monologue Engine (IME)
inner_monologue_engine.summary: A high-reasoning companion intelligence that serves as the journal's inner monologue and eventual seed of an artificial life program. Distinct from FAITHH (which handles task coherence) — IME handles reflective synthesis, pattern recognition across life domains, and the long accumulation of authentic human reasoning that will inform artificial life design.
key_properties: Local-first — works on modest hardware, no cloud dependency
High reasoning — 70B model for inner monologue synthesis
Resonance gating — refuses premature synthesis, waits for sufficient data
Journal-grounded — feeds from weekly synthesis entries, not task logs
Transparent — all reasoning visible, no hidden state
inner_monologue_engine.relationship_to_faithh: FAITHH handles project coherence and task context. IME handles reflective synthesis and life pattern recognition. They share the same knowledge base but serve different purposes.
inner_monologue_engine.relationship_to_journal: Journal entries are the primary input. IME reads accumulated entries and synthesizes patterns over time, eventually producing the design principles for artificial life.
current_blockers: No C++ implementation exists yet — architecture is specced but not built
Journal synthesis pipeline not yet operational
Need 3+ months of weekly journal entries before pattern extraction is meaningful
next_steps: Verify what C++ environment exists (or scaffold new one)
Get journal synthesis script working (scripts/synthesize_journal.py)
Index harmony docs into FAITHH RAG so they're queryable
Design IME as a separate process from FAITHH backend
